user_reported_bug: Retest bug #3 (planning pattern): sur un mois avec jours fériés, le pattern hebdomadaire de l'utilisateur doit être prioritaire sur les jours fériés. Nov 1 2026 (dimanche) doit être OFF (pas holiday). Nov 11 2026 (mercredi) doit être worked (pas holiday). Le nom du jour férié est indiqué dans le label mais ne remplace pas le statut worked/off.
summary: No relevant testing skill found. Backend-only retest verified the exact reported pattern-over-holiday precedence on /api/availability for a newly created Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00 bureau user: Nov 1 2026 returned off with Toussaint label, Nov 11 returned worked with Férié/Armistice label, and no holiday statuses were returned. However the requested no-pattern holiday fallback regression failed: a user created with no work_days/off_days returned off for Nov 1 and Nov 11 instead of holiday, so the overall focused verification is not_fixed.

critical.issue: Regression failure: for a newly created user with no weekly pattern (no work_days/off_days and weekly_pattern={}), public holidays no longer fall back to status='holiday'. 2026-11-01 returned status='off' label='OFF · Toussaint', and 2026-11-11 returned status='off' label='OFF · Armistice 1918'.

action_items: Preserve the current fixed behavior for users with a weekly pattern: schedule/off pattern must be evaluated before holiday and holiday should only be added to the label.

Fix the no-pattern fallback so days with no real/materialized schedule and no explicit weekly_pattern can still return status='holiday' on public holidays instead of synthesized off. Retest Nov 2026 with both patterned and no-pattern users.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/server.py availability() now correctly checks CP/RTT approved, pending, sched.off, and sched.shift before holiday fallback; this fixes the exact patterned-user precedence case.

Remaining regression appears caused by _entry_from_pattern() returning a synthetic off entry when weekly_pattern is empty. availability() cannot distinguish this implicit no-pattern off from an explicit schedule/pattern off, so the new sched.off branch masks holiday fallback for no-pattern users.
seed_data_creation: Created two transient QA users through POST /api/admin/users: one Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00 patterned user and one no-pattern user. Inserted three transient request rows directly for CP approved, RTT approved, and pending regression checks. Cleanup removed created users, schedules, requests, documents, badging, and notifications.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use /app/test_reports/bug_verification_21_backend_test.py. Main pattern precedence now passes: Nov 2026 returned worked=21, off=9, holiday=0; 2026-11-01 off label OFF · Toussaint; 2026-11-11 worked label Travail 09:00–17:00 · Férié (Armistice 1918). Status regression for past/cp_approved/rtt_approved/pending passed. No-pattern holiday fallback failed with holidays returned as off. Auth is MOCKED/custom X-Employee-Id.
rca_of_the_issue: The exact holiday-vs-weekly-pattern precedence was fixed by moving holiday fallback after schedule/request checks. The remaining regression is that _entry_from_pattern() treats an empty weekly_pattern as off for every day, and availability() applies sched.off before holiday fallback, so no-pattern users never reach the holiday fallback branch.
